Does Mathlib have any formalized combinatorics-on-words theory?

I'm building a library for combinatorics on words as part of a bigger project including words as List (Fin k), factors, powers/squares, morphisms, and eventually Thue's overlap-free and square-free theorems.

I just wanted to check before I invest a lot of time in it - searching yielded nothing specific to combinatorics on words. I'd also like to eventually propose part of it as a mathlib pr, and would appreciate any pointers!

Martin Dvořák said:

@Stepan Holub has something!

In mathlib, I have the Periodicity Lemma, which is somewhat related to Thue's stuff. Note, however, that Thue's theorems concern infinite words, which raises the question of how to bridge/relate the datastructures of finite vs. infinite sequences.

I also have a follow-up about multiperidoc words which is done both in Lean and Isabelle (a related book chapter is to be published soon). The code is not in mathlib yet, but it will possibly be there eventually.

With Stepan Starosta we have an extensive library on CoW in Isabelle. Most of the code still being about finite words, but it contains some material by Stepan Starosta about infinite words. In particular Sturmian words are quite directly related to Thue.
@Stepan Holub thanks! I've opened 2 basic PRs #41882 and #41915 if you want to take a look haha
